summary:
Set 120 Session 2 decides what to do about the drifted step statuses already on disk, and executes the operator's ruling: 271 lossless synonyms normalised, 15 semantically loaded entries preserved byte-for-byte.

(1) THE INVENTORY IS A COMMAND, NOT A QUERY, AND IT CONFIRMS THE SPEC. ai_router/step_status_drift.py measures 109 activity logs, 2,805 entries, 286 drifted (10.2%) across 24 files, split 271 lossless (completed 229, done 42) and 15 loaded (4 absent, 8 prose, 1 JSON array, 1 skipped, 1 complete-with-known-failures). Spec-mandated verdict on any discrepancy: there is none against the spec's AMENDED figures; the one wrong number this spec ever carried (the pre-amendment 'roughly a hundred session-set directories') was already corrected to 24 by S1, and 24 is what the command measures. Two facts the original one-off query missed, both about the query rather than the ruling: a 110th activity log exists outside docs/session-sets (the pinned UAT fixture, 2 further 'completed'), and the logs carry mixed CRLF/trailing-newline conventions with one ensure_ascii=False file.

(2) THE PREMISE WAS FALSIFIED, NOT ASSUMED, ON THREE SIGNALS. The ruling holds only if completed/done are pure synonyms wherever they appear, so the session hunted the counter-example: owning session never completed (0 hits), same step re-logged later as non-terminal (0 hits), step description asserts non-completion (1 hit). THE PREMISE STANDS. The negative result is only worth what the net was, so: the description signal first ran word-level (failed/failure/blocked/deferred), produced 38 hits, and all 38 were read in full -- every one incidental text ('0 failed' in a suite count, test_failure_injection.py in a file list, 'deferred to Set 062' as a scope note). Narrowing to phrases left one real hit, Set 061 S4 deferral-close, where 'cut short' describes the SET while the step itself recorded the deferral and closed VERIFIED. That reading is recorded in-module as an adjudication, so the check exits 0 today and still exits 2 the day a new counter-example appears.

(3) THE REWRITE IS BYTE-SURGICAL, BECAUSE A RE-SERIALIZE WOULD HAVE BROKEN THE RULING'S OWN ACCEPTANCE CONDITION. 108 of 109 logs are CRLF, 39 carry a trailing newline and 69 do not, and Set 028's was written ensure_ascii=False so it holds a literal arrow a default json.dump would escape. Parse-mutate-dump would have rewritten bytes in files it was asked not to touch, and made 'the loaded entries come out byte-identical' unevaluable because everything would have moved. The migrator instead locates each status member as a raw-text span, cross-checks those spans against what the parser sees (a file the scan cannot explain is REFUSED, never rewritten blind), replaces only the ruled ones, and asserts both that no byte outside them moved and that the reparsed document differs by exactly those statuses.

(4) THE RESULT IS VERIFIED FOUR WAYS, INCLUDING ONE INDEPENDENT OF THE TOOL. 271 tokens rewritten across 21 files; 15 loaded entries preserved. Beyond the migrator's own two internal proofs: git diff across the 21 migrated files is exactly 271 removed status lines and 271 added and nothing else; re-running --in-place changes 0 files, so an interrupted run is recoverable by re-running it; and the post-migration inventory reports drift down from 286 (10.2%) to exactly the 15 preserved entries (0.5%).

(5) BOTH VERIFICATION FINDINGS WERE THE SAME DEFECT CLASS, AND BOTH WERE REAL: INTENT DOCUMENTED, NOT ENFORCED. Round 1 (spec-conformance) found that --check-premise and --migrate were independent CLI branches, so a consumer -- invited by my own changelog entry -- could run --migrate --in-place on history that had never been through the check, laundering the exact outcome it exists to protect. Round 2 (supplementary completeness critic) found the same shape in a second place: I journaled the UAT-fixture exclusion and wrote 'deliberately out of scope' in the docstring, then implemented it as nothing at all -- it held only because the DEFAULT scan root happened to avoid it, and --scan is a supported flag. Both accepted. The premise check is now an enforced precondition at both entry points with no --force (the way past a flag is to read it and record the reading), and EXCLUDED_PATH_SEGMENTS enforces the fixture exclusion structurally on path segments, still reported so the residual stays a decision. Round 3 remediation-review: VERIFIED, 2 fix-accepted, 0 findings.

(6) THE FALSIFIERS FALSIFY, PROVEN BY MUTATION. 14 test functions / 17 cases. Both findings are planted rather than merely fixed, and both directions of the raw scan are planted as a look-alike pair (a stray status member the parser does not see is refused; an escaped status quoted inside a description is read as text). Mutation checks: swapping the surgical rewrite for a json.dump re-serialize fails 5 cases; widening the ruled scope to swallow skipped and complete-with-known-failures fails 6.
files_changed: docs/session-sets/*/activity-log.json (21 files, the 271 lossless tokens only)

reason.specifics: Session 3 is the set's terminal session and its largest: ship the single computed projection, give absence the explicit unknown/stale/unreadable states it currently hides, prove parity against session_checklist, and remove the <- here marker in the same pass. It depends on holding two sessions of context that are now on disk rather than in a model: which 15 entries were deliberately preserved and why they must render as an explicit unknown rather than a guess (S2's ruling), and why the vocabulary is four tokens and not five (S1's). Both are documented, so a different orchestrator is workable -- but S3 also inherits a live budget constraint that rewards continuity: the set's irony budget caps new tests at 40 across three sessions, S1 spent 19 and S2 spent 14, leaving 7 for a session with four progress keys. Judging what to cover in 7 functions is easier for someone who knows what the first 33 already assert. Same provider is fine because verification routes cross-provider and has been productive at it: three of this set's four verification rounds surfaced a real Major that the orchestrator had not seen.

notes.session_position: Session 2 of 3, NOT set-terminal. No change-log.md is authored here (it belongs to Session 3), and pathAwareCritique is deliberately absent from this set's configuration, so no critique artifact is owed at any point in the set. Nothing is published: the package stays at 1.0.0 (staged, operator-gated) and the Set 120 changelog section is [Unreleased].
notes.the_operator_ruling_and_what_this_sessio: The migration scope was ruled by the operator before this session opened (option (c), lossless synonyms only), and this session did not reopen it -- its job was to falsify the premise, report if it failed, and execute. Both the ruling and the one scoping call this session made on its own authority (excluding the pinned UAT fixture, on goal-over-letter: it is test data, not a record of a real session, and touching it would import an extension-test obligation this set's requiresE2E: false and standing decision 3 exclude) are journaled in decisions.jsonl. The ruling was journaled FIRST, before any file was rewritten, so it survives a failed migration.
notes.what_session_3_inherits: (a) The 15 preserved entries are S3's headline test case: 4 absent statuses (all Set 028), 8 prose blobs (Set 110) and 1 JSON array (Set 068), 1 skipped (Set 009), 1 complete-with-known-failures (Set 014). S3's explicit unknown / stale / unreadable states must render these honestly rather than guess, which is the whole reason they were not normalised. (b) The absent-status four are the concrete case for whether absence should also be refused at the writer -- S1 named this as a decision to make on purpose, and it is still open. (c) The step-status field is now clean enough that any remaining [?] in a rendered ledger is a TRUE signal about loaded data rather than noise, which is what makes the parity proof meaningful. (d) Test budget: 40 cap, 19 spent by S1 and 14 by S2, 7 remaining. (e) The spec notes that admitting skipped gets cheaper after S3 collapses the two readers -- still not S3's job, but S3 is what makes it a one-place change.
notes.residuals_named_not_hidden: (1) The pinned UAT fixture keeps its 2 'completed' tokens by decision; a future set that carves the extension can migrate it in the same pass that owns its tests. (2) The premise check's description signal is phrase-level and therefore not exhaustive -- it is the weakest of the three signals by design, since the two structural ones (session outcome, step re-logged non-terminal) are what actually carry the falsification. (3) Consumer repos with their own drifted history are not migrated by this session and are not obliged to migrate; the command is available and fail-closed if they choose to.
